Source B: (Quantitative data, hypothetical randomised trial) 2,400 Year 9 students: GPA change after a 50-minute online mindset lesson: lower-achieving students +0.10; higher-achieving students +0.01; control group 0.00.

Source C: (Method summary) A survey asked 500 students to rate how far they agreed that "intelligence can be developed" and correlated this with their grades (r = 0.12).

Using all the sources and your own knowledge, evaluate the claim that teaching a growth mindset improves learning. [15]
items.answer: B gives causal but small effects, mostly for lower achievers; C shows a weak correlation; A shows implementation problems; own knowledge: Blackwell et al. (2007) positive, Sisk et al. (2018) meta-analysis weak, replication concerns. Conclusion: modest benefits for some students when the school context supports the message.
